octo-feather-handoff.stdout:
usage: octo-feather-handoff [-h]
                            {encode,parked,resume-workspace,parent,repoint,report,results,prune-results,spawn,attempt}
                            ...

Encode a handoff record, or find a parked record in the caller's director and
lane logs. Kit-only stdlib json suffices; Herdr still owns transport. Encode
prints one JSON line for redirection, with string fields via --field KEY VALUE
and arbitrary JSON fields via --json-field KEY JSON. No handoff schema or
policy is imposed. parked TARGET LANES prints the latest parked line naming
TARGET by pane or name, among LANES/*.handoffs.jsonl and the director log
beside LANES (director.handoffs.jsonl; comms spec #session-state, #roles-
park), or exits 1 when none does. A lane line gains `lane` (its log's stem),
and one without a name is the supervisor: the lane's name. A director line
names its own general worker and gains no lane. resume-workspace reads a
worker's parked line on stdin and prints the workspace it resumes in: its
recorded parent's (`herdr agent get PARENT`) while that parent is live, else
the caller's HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID (comms spec #roles-park); an empty line when
neither. spawn [--ticket T] [--caller PANE] reads herdr-spawn's printed line
on stdin (name= role= tab= pane= cwd= contract= provider_session_id=) and
prints one spawn line for redirection into the lane hand-off log: {at, kind:
spawn, name, role, pane, cwd, session, ticket: T, else the name's part after
`<role>-` when it has one}. With --caller PANE (herdr-spawn passes its
caller's HERDR_PANE_ID) it prints nothing and appends the line to PANE's own
log in the caller's session state (octo-feather-state): the lane hand-off log
beside the lane record whose `supervisor` is PANE, else the director log when
director.toml's `pane` is PANE; a PANE owning neither records nothing (exit
0). parent PANE prints the caller's parent pane, resolved by identity at each
call (comms spec #say-parent: the parent survives park, restart and resume):
the hand-off log holding a spawn or worker-spawn line whose `session` is the
caller's OCTO_FEATHER_SESSION_ID (lane logs first, then the director log)
names it through its owner record, the lane record's `supervisor` or
director.toml's `pane`, as that record reads now, so a hand edit is what the
next call follows. PANE (the frozen OCTO_FEATHER_PARENT) when no such line or
no such key. Whether that pane is live is herdr-say's. report reads a worker's
report on stdin, for its `herdr-say --parent` (comms spec #notify-done): for a
worker role (OCTO_FEATHER_ROLE implementer, code-reviewer, corrector or
general-worker) whose spawn line `parent` finds, it appends the report (a `##
AT NAME (ROLE)` heading, UTC, then the report whole) to its result file beside
that log, `<log stem>.results/<session>.md` (lanes/<lane>.results/ or
director.results/), and prints the one-line notice herdr-say sends instead:
the file and the report's first line. Prints nothing (herdr-say sends the
report whole) for any other role or with no such line; a write that fails is
named on stderr, exit 1. results lists the caller's outstanding workers, read-
only: each spawn or worker-spawn line in the log HERDR_PANE_ID owns (as spawn
--caller finds it) whose session no later attempt line names, the latest per
session; one tab-separated line each: name, pane, state, result. State is
`live STATUS` while `herdr agent get NAME` finds it (its current pane shown),
`parked` when not and a parked line in that log names it, else `ended`;
`unknown (...)` when that lookup fails another way. Result is its result file
when one exists, else `ended, no result file` for an ended worker and `none
yet` otherwise. Exit 65 when the caller owns no log. prune-results removes the
director's result files (director.results/*.md) older than 7 days whose worker
(named by the director log's spawn line for that session) Herdr no longer
finds; each removal named on stderr. octo-feather-start runs it. A lane's
results dir moves with the lane at `octo-feather-lane archive`. repoint NAME
reads the line herdr-spawn printed for a resumed agent on stdin and writes its
pane= into NAME's record in the caller's session state: lanes/NAME.toml
`supervisor`, or director.toml `pane` for NAME `director`; only that key's
line, in place (added first when absent), every other line kept. No record:
nothing written (exit 0). octo-feather-start --resume runs it. attempt
--ended-unreported LOG PANE --partial X --recovery Y [--commit C] prints the
attempt line for a worker that ended without reporting (fields: comms spec
#handoff-fields, attempt): role, ticket, worker, session and duration_s come
from the latest spawn or worker-spawn line in LOG naming PANE. Refused,
nothing printed: exit 65 when no such line, or one without a session; exit 75
while `herdr agent get PANE` still finds the agent (close it first, so no
competing writer remains); exit 69 when that lookup fails another way.

positional arguments:
  {encode,parked,resume-workspace,parent,repoint,report,results,prune-results,spawn,attempt}

octo-feather-lane.stdout:
octo-feather-lane archive NAME   close lane NAME: move lanes/NAME.toml and
                                   lanes/NAME.handoffs.jsonl into lanes/archive/

The state dir is the one `octo-feather-state` prints (XDG_STATE_HOME, HERDR_SESSION).
Before moving any file `archive` runs the lane reflection, then the director reflection (`reflect`,
below); when either cannot run, the archive refuses naming the failed reflection, every file left in place.
`archive` creates lanes/archive/ if missing, moves each file byte-for-byte unchanged
and prints `archived: <file> sha256=<hex>` per file. A lane with no hand-off log gets one
from the reflection (its reflection line). It refuses, non-zero with every file left in
place, when the record is missing or either archive target already exists.


Archive of a merged lane (issue 1134; issue-lifecycle #gates-main-moved, comms #transport-close-space): a lane record
with a `pr` first asks the lane's post-merge record (`post-merge`, below) for that PR. Steps 1-3 not recorded ok, the
archive runs the routine itself (PR, the recorded head or else the PR's, the record's `repository` as --repo), its
lines printed, and re-executes itself on the kit install when step 3 moved the install this script runs from; still
